meta.subtitle: Maintainer picked ‘oku’ (Turkish ‘read!’ — the imperative). 3 chars, no Latin, no famous-product collision, distinctive token in the global package indexes.
meta.summary: Decided. ‘oku’ is the new name. Migration plan (CLI binary, skill name, package, repo, kit.json schema URLs, docs references) is a separate follow-up. Round-two exploration kept below for posterity.

blocks.summary: Decision: **oku** (Turkish, imperative of okumak — ‘read!’). Three chars. No Latin. No famous-product collision. Personal-cultural fit. ‘oku build’ / ‘oku init’ scan cleanly. Round-one and round-two artefacts kept below for the record.
bullets: Six directions explored — page/doc compound · essence words · knowledge metaphors · writing tools · short verbs/punch · Turkish roots.
New front-runners — pith (literal ‘to-the-point’), tome (knowledge body), oku (Turkish ‘read’, 3 chars).
Kept — pagekit, pageful, crisp from round one.
Dropped — every Latin/classical name + every collision with a famous product.
Decision is gated on PyPI / npm / GitHub availability — same as before.

blocks.title: Six naming directions — the design space
blocks.lead: Each card is a *direction*, not a single candidate. Reading them together shows the space we're working inside; the per-direction picks below are the strongest representatives.

cards.title: 1. page / doc / kit compound
items: Format-bound roots accepted — they describe the artefact.
‘kit’ encodes ready-to-use; ‘page’ encodes visual artefact.
Picks: pagekit, pageful, pagedeck, docink, inkpage.
Lowest brand-risk because the descriptor is honest.

cards.title: 2. essence / ‘just to the point’
items: Words that ARE the spec — ‘pith’, ‘crisp’, ‘terse’.
Short, vivid, distinctive. Highest match for the kit's stated philosophy.
Picks: pith, crisp.
Risk: ‘crisp’ shares with Crisp.chat; ‘pith’ is uncommon.

cards.title: 3. knowledge metaphor (English, not Latin)
items: Words that name what the kit stores — knowledge.
‘tome’ (a book), ‘lore’ (body of teachings), ‘saga’ (story-record).
Picks: tome, lore.
Strong brand surface; instantly evocative without Latin baggage.

cards.title: 4. writing tool
items: Names that ARE the implement — ‘ink’, ‘quill’, ‘nib’, ‘pen’.
Tactile + visual + minimalist.
Picks: ink, quill (nib as variant).
Risk: ‘ink’ namespace is busy; ‘quill’ shares with the Quill editor.

cards.title: 5. short punchy verb / sound
items: 1-syllable, fun-to-say words that scan as CLI verbs.
‘riff’ (musical improvisation), ‘pep’ (energy), ‘pop’ (generic).
Picks: riff, pep.
Risk: tone may read playful, not authoritative.

cards.title: 6. Turkish root (personal-cultural fit)
items: User is Turkish; English isn't the only naming language.
‘oku’ (read, imperative — ‘read this!’), ‘sayfa’ (page).
Picks: oku. 3 chars, instantly readable to TR speakers, distinctive abroad.
Risk: non-TR readers see an unfamiliar token; CLI namespace likely clean.

blocks.lead: All directions, all picks, scored on the same seven criteria. Chip filter on the verdict column.

blocks.title: New front-runners — detail cards
blocks.lead: The three new picks that rose above last round's compound family. Each has its own flavor — pick by what register you want.

blocks.content: Four characters. English noun: ‘the essential or central part of something’. Literally is the spec — the kit exists to make documentation that's just-to-the-point.

cards.title: Why it fits
items: Single word that names the kit's stated philosophy — concision, essence.
Pleasant to type; reads cleanly as a CLI verb.
Distinctive — no famous-product collision.
Brand surface: clean wordmark; tiny logo footprint.

cards.title: Risks
items: Uncommon English word — some readers won't know the meaning.
Two-letter combinations ‘ph’ + ‘th’ feel slightly literary.
Less ‘rich built-in’ vibe than pagekit; ‘pith’ leans toward minimal.

blocks.content: Four characters. English noun: ‘a large, scholarly book — a volume forming part of a larger work’. Old English / Middle English root (via Greek ‘tomos’, but anglicised long ago — not Latin). Names what the kit produces.

cards.title: Why it fits
items: Instantly conveys ‘a body of knowledge’ — matches the kit's role.
Short, distinctive, instantly memorable.
CLI: ‘tome build’, ‘tome init’ — flows as a sentence (‘build the tome’).
Reads as a brand, not a description.

cards.title: Risks
items: Slight ‘heavy book’ connotation — the kit's tone is lighter.
Greek root long-anglicised, but some readers may file it next to Latin in spirit.
Niche existing uses (a Discord bot ‘Tome’, several small libraries) — namespace check needed.

blocks.content: Three characters. Turkish — the imperative of ‘okumak’ (to read). ‘oku!’ = ‘read!’. The literal command form of what the kit asks the reader to do. Distinctive token in non-TR namespaces, instantly meaningful to the maintainer.

cards.title: Why it fits
items: Three characters — minimum CLI cost.
Cultural fit — maintainer is Turkish; the kit's identity carries that.
‘oku build’ — short, punchy, completely distinctive token.
Namespace likely clean: 3-letter Turkish words rarely collide with English-default tool indexes.

cards.title: Risks
items: Non-Turkish readers see an opaque token until they look it up.
Pronunciation drift in English (‘oh-koo’ vs ‘ah-koo’) needs a tagline ‘oku — Turkish for read’.
Trademark / SEO: ‘oku’ is also a Yoruba word, a Japanese word, etc. — meaning shifts by language but the spelling is stable.

blocks.title: CLI scan test — read each block out loud
blocks.lead: Same four commands across every front-runner.

blocks.source:
# pith
pith init   docs/plan.json
pith build
pith serve
pith check

# tome
tome init   docs/plan.json
tome build
tome serve
tome check

# oku
oku init    docs/plan.json
oku build
oku serve
oku check

# pagekit
pagekit init  docs/plan.json
pagekit build
pagekit serve
pagekit check

# pageful
pageful init  docs/plan.json
pageful build
pageful serve
pageful check

# crisp
crisp init    docs/plan.json
crisp build
crisp serve
crisp check

# riff
riff init     docs/plan.json
riff build
riff serve
riff check

# (baseline — today)
html-doc init docs/plan.json
html-doc build
html-doc serve
html-doc check

blocks.title: What the typing test shows
blocks.content: ‘tome build’ flows the best — full sentence shape. ‘pith build’ is punchy but slightly literary. ‘oku build’ is fastest to type, totally distinctive, with a one-line tagline. ‘pagekit build’ stays as the no-Latin compound option. ‘riff build’ is fun but the tone reads playful, not authoritative. ‘html-doc build’ remains the hyphen-friction baseline.

blocks.title: Rejected — refresher
blocks.lead: The reject list from round one carries over. Codex, Folio, Vellum, Lectern, etc., still out.

cards.title: Latin / classical family
items: Folio, Vellum, Lectern, Codex, Lectorium, Scriptorium, Quire, Recto, Verso, Limn, Imprint, Compendium, Marginalia, Lumen.
User: ‘not my culture’ — entire family pruned.

cards.title: Famous-product collisions
items: Codex (OpenAI Codex), Atlas (MongoDB), Stencil (Ionic), Astro, Hugo, Eleventy, Prism (kit dependency!), Slate, Quill (Quill editor).
Permanent search + conversation tax.

cards.title: Cute / fragile
items: Foli0, ReadMee, PaPage, htmldøc.
Reader has to learn the joke before the tool.

cards.title: Generic single English nouns
items: Read, Page, Doc, Site, Story, Book.
Too generic to brand or own.

blocks.title: Recommendation
blocks.lead: Fork in the road. Each step is a namespace gate.

steps.title: Check ‘tome’ on PyPI / npm / GitHub
steps.content: Strongest single-word pick. If clean (no big PyPI package, no popular npm), ship as ‘tome’. Best balance of metaphor strength + CLI ergonomics.

steps.title: If tome blocked, check ‘pith’
steps.content: Cleanest semantic match for the kit's stated philosophy. Slightly literary; the trade is conceptual fit > brand recognition.

steps.title: If pith blocked, check ‘oku’
steps.content: Personal-cultural fit. Three chars, clean namespace (Turkish words rarely collide), needs a one-line tagline.

steps.title: If oku blocked, fall back to ‘pagekit’
steps.content: Round-one lead. Compound that says what it is. Safest choice.

steps.title: If pagekit blocked, ‘pageful’ → ‘crisp’ → keep ‘htmldoc’
steps.content: The chain from round one still applies. Don't rename for a tied pick — the migration cost only pays out when the new name is meaningfully better than the current.

blocks.title: My pick
blocks.content: tome — short, English, knowledge metaphor, no Latin, no famous collision. Falls back to pith → oku → pagekit. The order is: best metaphor first, best personal fit second, safest compound last.

rows: Is ‘tome’ taken on PyPI / npm / GitHub?
Three-letter and four-letter names are usually claimed early. Check first; pick second.
One-line tagline: ‘oku — Turkish for read; the kit reads your JSON, builds your docs.’
If the tagline lands, the unfamiliarity becomes an asset (memorable). If not, fall through to ‘tome’.
Quick USPTO TESS + EUIPO search; software class 9 / 42
Avoid a name already filed in our space. Not for filing — just for due diligence.
Pronounceability across the user's daily languages (TR / EN / DE)
Say each finalist out loud in each language
‘tome’ reads cleanly everywhere; ‘pith’ has the ‘th’ sound that some non-EN speakers stumble on; ‘oku’ is TR-native, EN-foreign but stable.
‘tome’ reads as a brand; ‘pith’ as a quote; ‘oku’ as an imperative. Each implies a different visual identity.
Decide whether to ship a short alias regardless of name (‘pk’ for pagekit, ‘t’ for tome)
Short alias eliminates the typing-friction argument and lets the long name carry the brand.
